standard.title: Reflect to refine dramatic practice
standard.description: reflect on their own and others' drama or practices to refine and inform their use of elements of drama, conventions and/or approaches to shape and sustain dramatic action
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can reflect on their own and others' drama to inform choices when manipulating elements and conventions (Y7-8). They can seek, accept and respond to feedback, and develop understanding of human behaviours and emotions in performance contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on their own and others' drama or practices to refine and inform their use of elements of drama, conventions and approaches to shape and sustain dramatic action.

nodes.label: Analytical reflection on elements, conventions and approaches
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse their own and others' drama at the level of specific element, convention and approach choices — identifying what is working, what is not, and why.
nodes.minimum_width: Student produces a reflection that analyses at least two specific choices (element, convention, or approach) in their own or a peer's drama, with reasoning for each assessment.
nodes.typical_width: Students compare use of conventions to explore and challenge power and oppression across performance styles; they analyse and make choices about manipulating elements and experimenting with conventions (subtext, beats) to affect meaning; they shape their use of elements and conventions to achieve intended meaning.
wider: Students write, pod-cast or video-cast a critical analysis of their own rehearsal process — documenting decisions, testing alternatives, and evaluating outcomes
Students analyse how their own dramatic practice responds to (or resists) cultural influences, naming specific choices as culturally shaped
nodes.hinge_reason: Reflective practice at the analytical level — not just 'what happened' but 'why this choice and what was its effect' — is the mechanism through which Y9-10 students develop independent dramatic judgment; without it, refining is reactive rather than intentional.

response_modes.reason: Provide analytical frameworks — 'What was the intention? What choice was made? What was the effect? What would you change and why?' — to scaffold the move from descriptive to analytical reflection.

success_criteria: Student analyses at least two specific dramatic choices with reasoning — not just description
Student's reflection distinguishes intention from effect and addresses the gap between them

nodes.label: Using reflection to shape and refine practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use reflective analysis to make informed, documented refinements to their dramatic practice — demonstrating that reflection has changed specific choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Student documents at least one change to their dramatic practice that is explicitly motivated by reflective analysis.
nodes.typical_width: Students shape their use of elements, conventions and styles to achieve intended meaning or effect; they reflect on and evaluate how successfully intentions, meaning and effects were achieved; they draw lessons for future dramatic practice.
wider: Students maintain a reflective practice journal or portfolio across a substantial drama project, analysing how their thinking evolved across multiple iterations
Students engage in peer-critique sessions using a shared analytical framework, developing capacity to give and receive high-quality developmental feedback

response_modes.reason: Reflection-into-practice is the integration move at Y9-10: analysis informs choice, choice produces work, work is analysed again. Structured cycles of make-reflect-revise are the key pedagogical scaffold.
Building a repertoire of reflective approaches — personal journal, peer critique, video review, critical writing — gives students multiple lenses for examining their own practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of reflective tools and approaches available — written analysis, peer critique, performance documentation, critical comparison — is broad; students who use multiple approaches develop stronger metacognitive command of their own dramatic development.
success_criteria: Student documents at least one change to dramatic practice explicitly motivated by reflective analysis
Student evaluates the effect of that change on the drama's meaning or effectiveness
Student draws at least one lesson for future practice
